<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920368_theRebbe_469" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920368_theRebbe_469__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the header information for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbat Parshat Ki Tavo,</t>
    <t s="2">18 Elul 5727</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions why the verse says "Your people, Israel" as two separate entities, implying they are distinct concepts.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"Look down from Your holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless Your people, Israel."</t>
    <t s="1">And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, precisely analyzes in his maamar beginning with these words</t>
    <t s="2">[which he said on the first 18 Elul upon his arrival in the USA for the second time, with the intention of residing there,</t>
    <t s="3">and the determination of that 18 Elul was on Shabbat Parshat Ki Tavo,</t>
    <t s="4">as in this year]</t>
    <t s="5">the fact that it says "Your people, Israel,"</t>
    <t s="6">behold, the people of God</t>
    <t s="7">("Your people")</t>
    <t s="8">are Israel, and Israel are the people of God,</t>
    <t s="9">so why does it specify both?</t>
    <t s="10">This is also perplexing,</t>
    <t s="11">for from the fact that it says "Your people, Israel"</t>
    <t s="12">(and not "Your people Israel"),</t>
    <t s="13">it implies that "Your people" and "Israel"</t>
    <t s="14">(in this verse)</t>
    <t s="15">are two different matters.</t>
    <t s="16">And it needs to be understood</t>
    <t s="17">(as the Rebbe precisely analyzes in the maamar),</t>
    <t s="18">behold, the concept of Israel is above the concept of "Your people"</t>
    <t s="19">[and this is also understood from the fact that the name "people" indicates</t>
    <t s="20">(sometimes)</t>
    <t s="21">the opposite of praise,</t>
    <t s="22">and the name Israel is from the phrase "for you have striven with God and with men and have prevailed"],</t>
    <t s="23">yet here it places "Your people" before "Israel."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the two terms imply two distinct blessings, and questions the difference between them and why the blessing for "Your people" precedes that for "Israel."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that what is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="3">that from the fact that it says "Your people, Israel" it implies they are two matters,</t>
    <t s="4">is based on what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="5">regarding the verse</t>
    <t s="6">"concerning Shaul and concerning Yonatan his son, and concerning the people of God and concerning the house of Israel,"</t>
    <t s="7">that the verse separates the matter.</t>
    <t s="8">And based on this, it can be added,</t>
    <t s="9">that from the superfluous "et" we learn not only that "Your people" and "Israel" are two matters,</t>
    <t s="10">but also that in "and bless Your people, Israel" there are two matters,</t>
    <t s="11">a blessing for "Your people" and a blessing for "Israel."</t>
    <t s="12">And it needs to be understood the difference between these two blessings,</t>
    <t s="13">and that the blessing for "Your people" precedes the blessing for "Israel."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
